description: PostgreSQL 18 variable-length bit strings, typmods, casts, result types, ordering, and indexes
sql: CREATE TABLE type_matrix_bit_varying (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, flags VARBIT(9) UNIQUE);

INSERT INTO type_matrix_bit_varying VALUES ('empty', B''), ('zero', B'0'), ('two_zero', B'00'), ('zero_zero_one', B'001'), ('zero_one', B'01'), ('one', B'1'), ('one_long', B'100000000'), ('one_one', B'11');
SELECT id, flags FROM type_matrix_bit_varying ORDER BY flags;
SELECT B'1'::varbit(5) AS short_cast, B'101010'::varbit(5) AS truncated_cast, B''::varbit(5) AS empty_cast, B'101'::varbit::bit(5) AS fixed_cast, B'101'::bit(5)::varbit(2) AS varying_cast;

SELECT ~(B'1'::varbit) AS inverted, B'1'::varbit << 1 AS shifted, B'1'::varbit & B'0'::varbit AS bit_and, B'1'::varbit || B'0'::varbit AS concatenated, set_bit(B'1'::varbit, 0, 0) AS replaced, substring(B'101'::varbit FROM 1 FOR 2) AS sliced, overlay(B'101'::varbit PLACING B'1' FROM 2 FOR 1) AS overlaid;
SELECT id FROM type_matrix_bit_varying WHERE flags = B'100000000';
SELECT atttypmod, format_type(atttypid, atttypmod) FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = 'type_matrix_bit_varying'::regclass AND attname = 'flags';
UPDATE type_matrix_bit_varying SET flags = B'1010101010' WHERE id = 'empty';
